claims.statement: Meta documents a User Access Token, obtained through a login dialog that grants an app permission to act on a person's data, issued in short-lived and long-lived forms.

sources.supports: User access tokens let your app take actions in real time based on input from the user.
sources.locator: Access Tokens for Meta Technologies, User Access Tokens

sources.supports: Default User and Page access tokens are short-lived, expiring in hours, however, you can exchange a short-lived token for a long-lived token.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Only existence is established. The access-tokens page states that token length changes over time and gives no format grammar; it is not recorded here.
Short-lived and long-lived user tokens are described as lifetimes of one credential kind; whether they are distinguishable by form is not stated and no split is made.

Leads, not claims: one scanner rule artifact (Gitleaks, pinned in source github-com-gitleaks-gitleaks-d47395c7b2) treats strings starting with the literal prefixes EAAM or EAAC followed by 100 or more alphanumeric characters as a Facebook Page access token candidate, and another (Nosey Parker, source github-com-praetorian-inc-noseyparker-8d6f62ccdb) treats a longer literal older prefix as a generic Facebook access token. They name different token kinds, so no corroborated claim is made and no family attribution is drawn. A Meta page stating a token grammar would settle it.
